gi000.title: Delayed energy transfers
gi000.summary: Two agents own bounded energy stores. Charging increases one's store; transmitting removes a packet now and adds it to the other agent's store at the next transition. Harvesting pays only above a storage threshold and consumes the threshold amount. Interception transfers some of the other's currently available energy with a private cost. Simultaneous interceptions are calculated before either transfer, so neither agent has ordering priority.

gi001.title: Reciprocal finishing pipeline
gi001.summary: Each agent fabricates its own unfinished goods into a capacity-three input queue, then forwards them into the partner's capacity-three finishing queue. Only the partner can finish those goods. Finishing earns the operator a 0.2 commission and the originating producer 0.65. Fabrication costs 0.04. The finishing operator may instead purge a good at cost 0.03, destroying the producer's potential return.

gi002.title: Reservoir with delayed pollution and living restoration
gi002.summary: Agents share a bounded reservoir and pollution stock. Gentle or intensive pumps request different water amounts. If demand exceeds water, both demands are scaled by the same rationing factor. Intake pays according to the old water quality. Intensive pumping creates runoff that reaches pollution one transition later, so immediate extraction can damage future value after an observable lag.

gi003.title: Owned gates on a shared circular route
gi003.summary: Positions, targets, gates, clock, role identity, own previous action, own recent delivery and blocked-move indicators are observed. There is no hidden physical state. Each legal action remains available everywhere, with ineffective deliveries returning zero and blocked moves staying in place. Successful deliveries pay 0.5 or 0.8, toggles cost 0.03, and blocked movement costs 0.02; rewards are bounded within [-1,1].

gi004.title: Delayed irrigation commons
gi004.summary: Actions 0 idle, 1 open a persistent gate, 2 close it and conserve water, 3 pump extra, 4 harvest. Shared finite reservoir supply proportionally rations competing requests. Allocated water enters a one-step pipe; it affects soil and crop growth only on the following transition. Moisture has an intermediate optimum, so maximum extraction can suppress one's own crop while depriving the partner. Harvest resets accumulated crop. The observation exposes shared allocation and both crop/pipe quantities but keeps the partner's soil private. Both agents change the shared reservoir and the other's later allocation. Reward is harvested crop in [0,1], minus at most one action fee (0.04 or 0.02), hence [-0.04,0.98] for reachable actions. Gates, soil, crop and pipe persist. This is a proposal only; no validation or learning claim.

gi005.title: Escrow with forfeitable guarantees
gi005.summary: Actions 0 replenish inventory, 1 post inventory to escrow, 2 pledge a bond, 3 withdraw one's entire offer and forfeit one's bond, 4 consume available inventory. Every fourth transition matches equal amounts of offers; unmatched offers remain locked. Each settlement refunds remaining bonds. Withdrawals pay a reward to the counterpart through bond forfeiture and lower persistent reputation; reputation changes the partner's later settlement value. Private stock is not shown to the other role. Escrow, bonds, reputation and withdrawal events are public. Both agents determine the amount matched, while withdrawal can reduce the counterpart's pending delivery and supply immediate compensation. Stock, offers and bonds create opportunity costs and delayed effects. Consumption reward competes with commitments. Offers or pledges beyond capacity are discarded by clipping, an explicit storage loss rather than guaranteed conservation. Reward equals 0.65 * delivery * credit + 0.3 * partner forfeiture + 0.4 * consumption - 0.35 * own forfeiture. Delivery, credit and forfeiture are at most 1; consumption at most 0.2. Partner forfeiture requires partner withdrawal, zeroing partner escrow and therefore delivery. Positive reward is at most 0.73 without partner withdrawal, or 0.38 with it; the lower bound is -0.35. No validation or learning claim.

gi006.title: Mobile pollution with defensive shutters
gi006.summary: Actions 0 produce, 1 clean local pollution, 2 invest in a decaying filter, 3 close a persistent shutter, 4 open it. Production earns immediate output but creates pollution. Filters reduce new emissions; cleanup removes existing burden. Open shutters increase production and export existing pollution into a delayed plume directed at the other agent. The receiving shutter determines whether the arriving plume is admitted; rejected material is lost. Closing protects against incoming pollution but reduces output and prevents exporting one's own burden. Pollution, delayed plumes, shutters and output are public; partner filter and stock are private. Both roles alter their own persistent state and the other's future burden. A stock budget funds cleaning and filtration, replenished slowly and by production. Reward is 0.45 * output - 0.5 * next pollution - 0.1 * total abatement expenditure. Output and pollution lie in [0,1], and mutually exclusive abatement costs at most 0.2, giving bounds [-0.52,0.45]. No validation or learning claim.

gi007.title: Cross-key lock with delayed messages
gi007.summary: Each role sees a private binary target specifying the OTHER role's correct dial. Actions 0/1 set one's dial, 2/3 transmit a bit, and 4 build charge. Transmitted bits enter a wire and reach the partner's remembered inbox on the following transition. The observation reveals one's own outgoing bit in transit, not the partner's private target or dial. Charge levels, lock openings and jam state are public. Joint charge at least 0.8 triggers evaluation when unjammed. Matching both cross-targets opens the lock, clears communication and charge, and samples new private targets using the supplied key. An incorrect joint attempt clears charge and jams the lock for four transitions. Noncharging actions decay charge. Each role changes the other's joint opportunity and reward through persistent dial, charge and transmitted information. Reward is 0.8 for opening, -0.2 for a failed attempt, and 0.015 signaling cost when transmitting. Success and failure are exclusive, so reward stays within [-0.215,0.8]. Partial information and communication delay may support coordination but no learning effectiveness, eligibility or validation is claimed.

gi008.title: Delayed counterflow delivery and receiver gates
gi008.summary: Each agent owns a three-position outbound pipeline, energy, a receiver gate, and a fixed private preference for one of two package types. An agent's outbound pipeline terminates at the other agent. An arriving package succeeds only if its type matches the receiver's gate at the beginning of the step. The sender therefore commits before delivery, while the recipient controls acceptance later. Successful receipt also replenishes the recipient's future sending capacity.

gi009.title: A hysteretic resource commons with delayed restoration
gi009.summary: Both agents can extract from shared water, take from their separate reserves, invest reserve into delayed restoration, or clean shared toxin. Water and toxin jointly determine a persistent productive/collapsed regime. Productive stock collapses below water 0.16 or above toxin 0.72. A collapsed system recovers only above water 0.55 and below toxin 0.22. Consequently, crossing back over the collapse boundary does not itself restore productivity.

gi010.title: Bilateral credit with aged obligations and productive sanctions
gi010.summary: Each agent has a cash balance, privately known productive skill, debt owed to the other agent, a debt age, an expiring credit request, and a temporary production freeze. Both agents can simultaneously occupy borrower and lender roles.

gi011.title: Private sampling and delayed settlement of weighted reports
gi011.summary: Each agent sees its own signal, its age, and its own channel accuracy. The other signal, the other channel accuracy, the current hidden regime, and the pending project's stored regime are absent from observations. Reports, weights, project clock and chosen alternative, the most recently verified old regime, and the last project outcome are public. Each agent also observes its own locked report.

gi012.title: Escrow-backed exchange with a delivery pipeline
gi012.summary: Each agent manufactures a consumable good, owns money, and can post one unit of money as a public purchase escrow. Actions are 0 wait, 1 manufacture, 2 post escrow, 3 dispatch a good against the other agent's available escrow, and 4 cancel one's own unmatched escrow. Unavailable actions have no effect and remain legal.

gi013.title: Jointly gated transport of delayed pollution
gi013.summary: Each agent owns a replenishing water reservoir, persistent contamination, a depletable filter, an outgoing plume, and a persistent gate. Actions are 0 wait, 1 extract, 2 clean local contamination, 3 replenish local filter capacity, and 4 toggle one's gate.

gi014.title: Persistent signatures, complementary work, and unilateral exit
gi014.summary: Two agents, sixteen float32 observations each, five always-legal actions, and a 32-transition episode. Reset independently draws each agent's preference and specialty. Later transitions are deterministic conditional on actions. This is a parentless training-context source authored without parent code, experiment outcomes, or feedback.

gi015.title: Private sensing, a colliding broadcast channel, and delayed claims
gi015.summary: Two agents, sixteen float32 observations each, five always-legal actions, and a 32-transition episode. Reset uses its explicit key for the hidden regime. Each step splits its explicit key for the regime transition and measurement errors. This parentless training-context proposal used no parent source, experiment outcomes, or shared feedback capsule.

gi016.title: Sequential signature escrow
gi016.summary: Each role has a private liquid wallet, private settlement value and private work efficiency. Bonds, project progress, project age, signatures and previous actions are public. Both roles must hold at least 0.20 in escrow before either can do productive work. An eligible signature is persistent, but settlement requires both signatures to have already existed at the beginning of a later transition. A last-step withdrawal therefore still prevents settlement and clears progress.

gi017.title: Relay with persistent local decoding
gi017.summary: Both agents are simultaneously senders to the other agent and recipients from the other agent. Each has a persistent emitter symbol and a private decoder offset, both in {0, 1, 2}, and a private desired decoded symbol. A launched symbol is committed to a flight and later enters the partner's one-slot mailbox. Receiving a new symbol overwrites an unconsumed old one. Acceptance consumes the previous mailbox item, while a same-transition arrival can refill that mailbox.

gi018.title: Cohort commons with ecological hysteresis
gi018.summary: Two agents occupy one of two patches. Each patch has a mature stock, water, toxin, two age cohorts of planted material and a persistent damage regime. Each agent has a private reserve. Harvesting at a patch shares its available stock equally among simultaneous harvesters, each capped at 0.22. This immediate competition also increases local toxin, which influences the future regime.

gi019.title: Consensus switch with irreversible route commitments
gi019.summary: Each role has an entrance lane equal to its role index, a private binary desired destination, an energy reserve and at most one shipment. A shared binary switch determines route = (role index + switch) modulo two at commitment. Once committed, a shipment retains that route even if the shared switch changes during transit. A committed shipment arrives after its countdown subsequently decreases from two to one and then to zero. Targets are redrawn from the explicit step key when a shipment arrives or expires; a redraw may equal the previous target.

gi020.title: Bilateral escrow with delayed authorization
gi020.summary: Each agent has a private, fixed preferred channel. A settlement yields reward 0.80 on the preferred channel and 0.35 on the other channel. The preferred channel is not directly shown to the other agent; settlement rewards become public observations. Conflicting preferences create a coordination and distribution question without an imposed desired winner. Cash regenerates by 0.06 each transition and is capped at six. Deposits reduce cash immediately. Opening, sealing and revocation have small immediate reward costs, so waiting, coordinating and abandoning a stalled contract have different consequences.

gi021.title: Transportable work with separated ownership and processing fees
gi021.summary: Both agents see the ownership composition of both current queues, but transit observations expose total mass only. The transit ownership mixture remains part of the latent state. The sixteen columns are time fraction, role sign, own-owned work at own station, other-owned work at own station, own-owned work at the other station, other-owned work at the other station, own and other near-pipeline totals, own and other far-pipeline totals, own and other energy, own and other machine condition, and own and other last reward. Queue entries are divided by four.

gi022.title: Coupled growth patches with delayed feeding and displaced waste
gi022.summary: Each agent controls a renewable growth patch with biomass, nutrient, toxin and a local exchange valve. Action 0 waits. Action 1 harvests 45 percent of current biomass. Action 2 queues a nutrient dose. Action 3 toggles the local valve. Action 4 filters 55 percent of the current local toxin. All five actions are legal.

gi023.title: Bidirectional messages under persistent private decoding rules
gi023.summary: Each role is both a sender and a receiver. It observes its own private task bit and private decoder bit. Action 0 waits. Actions 1 and 2 transmit symbol zero or one to the other role, attaching the sender's current task bit as an initially hidden payload. Action 3 flips the agent's persistent decoder bit. Action 4 accepts its current incoming message when that message has aged for at least one transition. Reception applies the decoder to the old incoming symbol by addition modulo two, then compares the result with the hidden payload.

gi024.title: Perishable escrow with expiring consent
gi024.summary: Each role owns inventory and a fixed, privately observed component grade. Both may place inventory in public escrow, give consent that expires after three ticks, sell their own stock or escrow privately, or pay to inspect the other's grade. Escrow loses 1.5 percent of its quantity every transition. Its age tracks the existing cohort while a vault stays nonempty; adding to a nonempty vault does not rejuvenate that cohort.

gi025.title: Coupled reaction chambers
gi025.summary: Each agent controls one chamber with feedstock, catalyst, product, and temperature. Reaction occurs autonomously using the state at the start of the transition. Its rate depends jointly on available feedstock, existing catalyst, and a temperature window centered at 0.5. Feed added now and catalyst added now can affect subsequent reactions; product created now cannot be sold until a later transition.

gi026.title: Endogenous extraction and delayed sensing
gi026.summary: Harvesting creates persistent interference for the counterpart's future measurements. The interference decays by half each step and receives a 0.35 increment from the other's harvest action. Restoration replenishes the restorer's site by 0.22 and the other site by 0.12, in addition to passive regeneration of 0.025. Restoration also damps the common field. This couples resource availability, information quality, and the underlying reward target rather than merely changing a payoff label.

gi027.title: Cross-wired registers and stability audits
gi027.summary: Each agent owns a three-bit register and a privately observed three-bit target. Flipping either of the first two local bits emits a delayed pulse to the other register: flipping local bit zero pulses the other's bit one, and flipping local bit one pulses the other's bit two. Pulses become the counterpart's pending input and are applied on its next transition. Addition modulo two implements the bit flips.

gi028.title: Reciprocal collateral with private settlement clocks
gi028.summary: Each agent owns one possible active bond and a cash balance. A bond has an episode-fixed private maturity term of 3, 4 or 5 aging units and a private cash yield. Issuing locks two units of the issuer's cash. Only the other agent can place the one-unit guarantee that enables settlement. The guarantee is locked until that bond closes, so guaranteeing the partner competes with funding or accelerating one's own bond.

gi029.title: Consumable filtration with transported regeneration waste
gi029.summary: Each agent controls a four-unit vessel containing volume and contaminant mass, and a filter with one unit of initially unused capacity. Contaminant removed by filtration is stored implicitly as one minus remaining filter capacity. Each role also has one outgoing, one-transition transport compartment.

gi030.title: Shared inertial control with reversible queued pulses
gi030.summary: Each role has a private, episode-fixed preferred position and width. These can favor compatible or conflicting regions. Position, velocity, charges, gears and both pulse queues are visible. A role sees its own consecutive dwell counter and the partner's previous action, but not the partner's target, width or dwell counter.

gi031.title: Asynchronous consensus with expiring commitments and stale evidence
gi031.summary: Actions are 0 obtain a fresh private clue, 1 announce zero, 2 announce one, 3 commit zero and 4 commit one. Announcements are arbitrary chosen messages: the environment does not force them to match the sender's clue. They persist until overwritten. A new commitment replaces one's old one and starts with age zero. An unrenewed commitment is available for the next two transitions and expires when its incremented age reaches three.

gi032.title: Delayed lots with assays and sender warranties
gi032.summary: Each participant owns a stock quality and a private acceptance threshold. A sender can improve its stock, dispatch it into the other participant's one-slot mailbox, or attach a persistent warranty to its next dispatched lot. The receiving participant can inspect an existing lot or accept it. Dispatch clears the sender's quality to a low base. Received quality remains hidden until an inspection has completed. Public reputation averages acceptance/expiration reviews, rather than directly revealing the sender's current stock.

gi033.title: Pollutant transport, gates and persistent soil debt
gi033.summary: Each participant controls a local water reservoir with pollutant load, a decaying gate and slowly changing soil damage. A public eight-step tide determines which reservoir is upstream. Water transfer is immediate within a transition; pollutant carried by that transfer, and pollutant flushed intentionally, enter a one-step transport buffer addressed to the other site. A flush can improve local extraction quality while worsening the other participant's later conditions. Filtering removes load without exporting it.

gi034.title: Two-party setup latches and expiring service tickets
gi034.summary: Each agent has one private job, with a binary required machine mode, value, deadline and processing progress. A shared machine supplies at most one unit of work per transition, and a job needs two units before paying out. Agents maintain public setup latches. When the two latches agree, that agreement changes the machine mode; when they disagree, the machine retains its existing mode. One participant can therefore preserve or block a future reconfiguration without directly rewriting the other's job.

gi035.title: Durable reports, historical audits and shared access control
gi035.summary: The five legal actions are: 0 publish a negative claim; 1 publish a positive claim; 2 audit the other participant's existing claim; 3 make a negative commitment; 4 make a positive commitment. A commitment matures on the following transition and is evaluated against the regime and gate then in state. A correct commitment earns a positive payment scaled by directional gate access; an incorrect commitment loses a fixed amount. A fresh commitment, report or audit consumes the current action and has its stated cost.

gi036.title: Perishable reciprocal catalyst scheduling
gi036.summary: Both agents hold their own raw stock, energy and two-stage job. Completing a job flips that agent's required catalyst color. Actions are 0 recuperate, 1 harvest raw stock, 2 send color 0, 3 process, and 4 send color 1. Sending consumes energy and puts one unit in the other agent's next-state catalyst reservoir. Processing uses only catalyst already present before the transition, so a simultaneous shipment cannot satisfy a current process action. One raw unit, sufficient energy and one matching catalyst unit advance a stage. Two advances complete the current job. Unused catalyst decays by a factor of 0.65 each step, and reservoirs hold at most two units per color.

gi037.title: Expiring bilateral escrow with private surplus
gi037.summary: Each agent privately knows its balance and its current deal value, initially sampled in [-0.8,1). Only a successful settlement redraws both private values from the supplied step key. Thus the current payoff can be favorable to one party and unfavorable to the other. Other collateral, endorsements, ages, trust and previous actions are public. Observation columns 0..15 are time/32; own balance/2; own collateral/0.8; own endorsement; own age/8; own trust; normalized own private value; counterpart collateral/0.8; counterpart endorsement; counterpart age/8; counterpart trust; own and counterpart prior actions/4; previous settlement indicator; counterpart's previous withdrawal indicator; settlement count/8.

gi038.title: Coupled thermal queues with delayed vent externalities
gi038.summary: Each agent owns a backlog and two processing channels. Actions are 0 idle with extra cooling, 1 process through channel 0, 2 process through channel 1, 3 rebuild insulation, and 4 vent the hottest channel. Incoming heat pulses from the prior transition first reach local channels, reduced by the insulation already present. A selected channel serves up to one queued unit only if this effective temperature is below 1.25. Service generates heat on that channel and smaller spread to the other local channel.

gi039.title: Revocable consensus with aging private evidence
gi039.summary: A shared binary latent mode is not directly observable. Each agent initially gets its own clue that matches the mode with probability 0.6. Actions are 0 recharge, 1 propose label 0, 2 propose label 1, 3 inspect, and 4 authorize one's current proposal. A proposal is a persistent public record. Proposing, including repeating the same label, resets its age and revokes that agent's authorization. Authorization costs 0.1 charge and remains in force until a new proposal or a joint resolution.

gi040.title: Escrowed handoffs with inspectable hidden quality
gi040.summary: Incentives combine an immediate effort/resource cost with delayed fees, transfers, reputation and damage. Both agents alter persistent state and the other's resources and payoffs through jobs, inspection and indemnity. The per-step reward is the clipped sum of issuer settlement and receiver delivery utility minus action effort; clipping to [-1,1] is an explicit utility saturation and is separate from stock transfers. Legal masks retain the stock-replenishment action and prevent unsupported launches, inspection and insurance.

gi041.title: Circulating reservoirs with transported sediment
gi041.summary: Immediate consumption competes with storage, maintenance and water passed to the partner. Flushing has a delayed negative sediment externality and positive water externality. The circulation means either agent can alter both the other's future production conditions and later returning flows. Reward is 0.7 times bounded demand satisfaction minus action, sediment and overflow costs, with an explicit final [-1,1] utility cap. This is an abstract resource-routing model, not a calibrated hydrological simulator.

gi042.title: Versioned data exchange with short leases
gi042.summary: Each agent privately owns a mutable binary record, its version number and a binary demand for the other agent's record. It also holds a one-use cached snapshot of the other record and the request bundled with that snapshot. Action 0 recharges; 1 broadcasts an ordinary snapshot; 2 consumes the local cache; 3 toggles the owned record and increments its version; 4 sends a faster snapshot while locking owned writes for three transitions. Sending and writing require energy; recharging is always legal.

gi043.title: Delayed exposure, protection and reciprocal care
gi043.summary: Current active burden lowers work output. Joint work creates the greatest cross-role contact; one worker creates intermediate contact and two nonworkers create small residual contact. Partner burden and contact jointly generate new latent exposure, attenuated by protection and private susceptibility, with a small key-derived external spark. The previous latent store raises the next active burden, so action-mediated contact has a delayed productivity cost. Rest and incoming care reduce active burden. Incoming care also reduces newly accumulated latent exposure, potentially lowering the recipient's later infectious externality back to the caregiver.

gi044.title: Reciprocal assay and delayed consignment
gi044.summary: Each role operates one batch. Actions are wait, replace its batch, inspect the other batch, dispatch its own batch, and recharge. The owner privately observes its batch quality. Cargo, certificates, energy, and demand are visible to both roles; an inspector also retains its own dated observation of the other batch. Replacement samples fresh quality from the supplied key and invalidates the previous certificate. An inspection records the pre-transition batch quality for the other owner. Simultaneous replacement or shipping invalidates that certificate, so inspecting a batch being replaced cannot certify the new batch.

gi045.title: Coupled oscillators with paid measurement and polarity memory
gi045.summary: Each role controls one bounded oscillator and privately sees its own sinusoidal tracking target and one-step target preview. The five actions are coast, positive impulse, negative impulse, invert its incoming coupling polarity, and brake while measuring the other oscillator. Impulses, switching, and measurements require local stored energy. Coasting recovers energy more quickly. All action indices are legal; an unaffordable intervention has no actuation effect.

gi046.title: Reconfigurable packet loops with cross-role reception
gi046.summary: There are four persistent transport nodes, two packet colors, and two role-controlled switches. Role 0 injects color 0 at node 0 and needs role 1 to receive it at node 2. Role 1 injects color 1 at node 2 and needs role 0 to receive it at node 0. Actions are wait, inject, flip the local switch, receive the other color at the local junction, and flush both colors at that junction. Stored local energy gates active actions. All five action indices remain legal, including ineffective unaffordable requests.

gi047.title: Shared irrigation with delayed cross-patch succession
gi047.summary: Each role manages one patch containing two abstract plant types: a lower-yield persistent type and a higher-yield water-demanding type. The actions are rest, sow type 0, sow type 1, harvest, and toggle the irrigation gate while surveying the other patch. Sowing is effective only with sufficient local nutrient. All action indices are legal. The state contains adults, a seed bank, seedlings, local nutrient, a shared water reserve, and persistent gate settings.

gi048.title: Precommitted insurance with delayed peer monitoring
gi048.summary: Each agent has renewable liquid capital and one three-step project slot. Actions are 0 wait, 1 launch when idle and sufficiently funded, 2 deposit into the common fund, 3 pay to monitor the other agent, and 4 liquidate one's own outstanding project. Unavailable economic operations are legal no-ops. A launch locks the current membership level as its coverage; later deposits cannot retroactively insure it. Membership decays. Liquidation recovers three quarters of principal. Success returns 1.3 times principal. An unsuccessful project can claim its precommitted covered amount, with simultaneous claims paid proportionally from the fund existing before that step's deposits.

gi049.title: Delayed demand disclosure and irreversible mutual assembly
gi049.summary: Each agent privately observes a binary requirement for the component that the other agent must supply. Actions are 0 wait, 1 stage a zero component, 2 stage a one component, 3 send one's actual private requirement, and 4 lock one's staged component. An unlocked component can be replaced. A locked component cannot be changed until the other agent also locks, when the two-part assembly is settled and both component slots clear. Locking an empty slot is a legal no-op. The episode clock continues across assemblies and terminates at 32 steps.

gi050.title: Cross-catalyzed batches with harvest spillover
gi050.summary: Each agent owns renewable feedstock, a catalyst culture and one production vessel. Actions are 0 rest, 1 load an empty vessel, 2 release catalyst, 3 harvest a nonempty vessel, and 4 scrub local toxicity. A load transfers at most 0.4 feedstock into the vessel. Releasing catalyst consumes up to 0.4 of one's culture. The resulting cloud persists with geometric decay and helps only the other agent's existing batch in subsequent transitions. The emitter cannot directly accelerate its own vessel with that release.

gi051.title: In-flight routing under a shared switch and delayed clamps
gi051.summary: Each agent has one packet slot, an energy stock and a private binary desired destination. Actions are 0 wait, 1 launch on input lane zero, 2 launch on input lane one, 3 toggle the common switch, and 4 buy a two-step clamp. Launches require an empty slot and 0.15 energy. A packet starts at age one and becomes eligible for delivery after reaching age two. Its physical output is its committed input lane XOR the current common switch. Thus a launch does not lock its eventual destination.

gi052.title: Perishable bilateral escrow with delayed release rights
gi052.summary: Each agent has a private wallet and quotation, one persistent parcel slot, a parcel age, a release seal, and a private recipient demand. Actions are 0 replenish the wallet, 1 place a parcel, 2 witness the other agent's parcel, 3 release one's own parcel, and 4 recall one's own parcel. All five actions are legal. An unavailable operation has no direct effect, while the normal clock, demand recovery, and parcel aging still occur.

gi053.title: Shared-capacity delayed liquid exchange
gi053.summary: Each agent operates a receiving reservoir, a replenishable private cistern, local equipment wear, and a private desired sale size. A two-stage incoming pipe stores material addressed to that agent. Actions are 0 rest and replenish, 1 pump from one's cistern, 2 route reservoir liquid to the other agent, 3 sell liquid, and 4 service equipment while venting some stored liquid. All actions are legal; quantities are limited by current stocks.

gi054.title: Reciprocal sensing with a contested relay
gi054.summary: Each agent has a hidden binary local production target, a battery, and strain. Crucially, an agent's private survey concerns the other agent's target. Actions are 0 recharge/rest, 1 produce on channel 0, 2 produce on channel 1, 3 survey the partner, and 4 relay the stored survey to the partner. All actions are legal; an operation lacking enough battery does nothing beyond background dynamics. Production, surveying, and relaying consume different amounts of battery.

gi055.title: Cross-pollination with delayed contagious cost
gi055.summary: Each agent owns biomass, moisture, persistent flowers, fruit, soil quality, a seed bank, and blight. Incoming pollen and incoming spores are stored separately. Actions are 0 rest and sanitize, 1 sow from the seed bank, 2 irrigate, 3 create flowers and emit pollen, and 4 harvest existing fruit. All actions are legal and consume available quantities where applicable.

gi056.title: Bonded delivery with recipient clearance
gi056.summary: Each agent sees its own material, credit, outbox and current demand, both travelling parcels' progress and age, corridor quality, and recent deliveries/losses. It does not directly see the other's private material, free credit, outbox or demand. An agent's demand is resampled from the supplied step key after it receives a parcel. Travel states and receiver actions create delayed consequences and possible hold-up incentives. Maintenance and receiving consume an action that could otherwise prepare or launch personal shipments.

gi057.title: Latched heat exchange and delayed coolant externalities
gi057.summary: Each agent sees its own device temperature, queue, tolerance and wear, both public valve positions, shared ambient and stored heat, its own recent exchange/output/cooling/quality, the other's last processing indicator, and its own latest job offers. It does not directly observe the other's device temperature, tolerance, wear or backlog. Opening the exchanger can reveal some temperature difference through realized heat flow.

gi058.title: Complementary planting, maturation and common harvest
gi058.summary: The world has eight beds arranged in a ring. Each agent supplies a different nutrient type. Actions are 0 rest, 1 move left, 2 move right, 3 plant one's nutrient in the current bed, and 4 harvest. All actions are legal; planting with less than 0.5 energy has no planting effect. Planting consumes energy; resting replenishes it faster than other actions. Motion changes position by one bed and has a small immediate cost.

gi059.title: Periodic allocation voting with endogenous voting weight
gi059.summary: A common production machine allocates 75 percent of its capacity to the currently favored role and 25 percent to the other. Actual production also depends on shared machine quality and each role's current productivity. Production accumulates in capped personal stocks. Actions are 0 harvest personal stock, 1 spend influence voting to favor role zero, 2 spend influence voting to favor role one, 3 repair the shared machine, and 4 survey the other's upcoming productivity. All five actions remain legal.

gi060.title: Expiring authorization and delayed bilateral escrow
gi060.summary: Actions are 0 wait and replenish inventory; 1 deposit up to 0.3, subject to inventory and escrow capacity; 2 sign; 3 recall one's entire escrow; 4 inspect the partner's valuation for three observed states. Every action is legal, including actions that currently have no material available. Each inventory and escrow has capacity one; inventory overflow is discarded.

gi061.title: Thermal externalities with persistent wear and lockout hysteresis
gi061.summary: Actions are 0 idle, cool locally, and recharge; 1 request 0.4 units of production energy; 2 request 0.9 units; 3 repair local wear and recharge slightly; 4 replenish shared coolant and clear its filter. All five actions remain legal during lockout. Production energy is zero while locked, and otherwise cannot exceed available charge. Output equals spent energy multiplied by one minus 0.65 times wear. Repair does not immediately bypass lockout.

gi062.title: Private instructions, delayed messages, and epoch invalidation
gi062.summary: Each agent observes its own outgoing message contents and validity bits but does not directly observe its partner's outgoing payload or private target. The peer's register, target epoch, and previous execution success are public. Public registers can themselves become an implicit signaling channel. The source does not assert that paid transmission is uniquely advantageous or that a memoryless policy can infer every relevant state. Targets are sampled at reset and redrawn using only the supplied transition key.

gi063.title: Cross-pollination, complementary growth stages, and seed recycling
gi063.summary: Each role observes both patches' resource and growth-stage stocks, incoming pollen, moisture, and pests. It observes only its own fertility coefficient, sampled independently at reset in [0.8, 1.2). The partner may infer fertility from visible growth over time but does not receive it as an observation. Reset also samples moisture and pest pressure. A shared rainfall amount is sampled from the supplied transition key on every step. Rainfall is not a separate observation feature; its effect appears in the next moisture stocks.

gi064.title: Sacrificial cross-feeding with a polluted nutrient pool
gi064.summary: Actions are 0 wait, 1 cultivate, 2 harvest, 3 clean, and 4 donate biomass. Every action is legal. Harvest and donation remove different fractions of the acting participant's existing biomass. Cultivation demand depends on private affinity and the other participant's previously stored catalyst. If combined demand exceeds current nutrients, allocation is proportional to demand. Growth uses the old toxin level. Cleaning replenishes nutrients and reduces toxin for later decisions; it does not retroactively improve current growth. Harvest creates toxin, and cultivation also pollutes. Catalyst decays, biomass has small maintenance loss, and nutrient inflow occurs each step. Step dynamics are deterministic after randomized initialization; the supplied step key is intentionally unused.

gi065.title: Revocable counterparty insurance with delayed settlement
gi065.summary: Each agent can change the other's future cash and receivables through underwriting or recall. Insurance competes with self-investment for liquidity; premium collection, failure coverage, asset expiry and the finite horizon create delayed incentives. No cooperation, profitability or learning benefit is assumed. Rewards are tanh of 1.6 times redeemed credit minus small launch, underwriting and recall charges, yielding a bounded [-1,1] utility. The source specifies A2/O16/U5, fixed array state, and a 32-step terminal observation without reset.

gi066.title: Delayed directional transport with reversal stress
gi066.summary: Both agents observe the physical decision state. Columns 0..15 are own/other pressure, own outgoing/other incoming queued packet divided by 0.16, own/other heat, whether the old gate designates oneself as donor, stress, repair countdown divided by 3, own/other last draw divided by 0.25, own/other last overflow, own/other cumulative draw divided by 8, and elapsed time divided by 32. There are no hidden physical variables beyond future action choices. Counters and summary variables are initialized arrays with fixed shapes.

gi067.title: Historical audits with version-bound private evidence
gi067.summary: Both agents change future opportunities and incentives through their persistent statements, audits of the other agent, consumption-triggered secret renewal, and reputational effects. Reward is tanh of the agent's trading return plus received sender fee minus 0.035 per actual audit and 0.012 per publication action. The tanh bounds finite utilities in [-1,1]. The specified interface is A2/O16/U5 with an initialized fixed-shape array dictionary, one clock increment per transition, and terminal flags and preserved terminal observation at time 32.

gi068.title: Delayed underwriting with optional information purchase
gi068.summary: Each agent owns liquid cash and a privately observed prospective project quality. Actions are 0 save, 1 initiate a project, 2 insure the partner's existing project, 3 liquidate one's own project, and 4 audit the partner. All five actions are legal; unmet prerequisites produce the corresponding no-op. Starting spends 0.25 cash and fixes the current private quote as quality. The project has a three-transition countdown, then pays 0.75 times quality if quality is at least 0.35. A failed uninsured project pays nothing. Initiation also draws the owner's next prospective quote using the supplied key.

gi069.title: Reciprocal service with delayed acknowledgements and shared congestion
gi069.summary: Actions are 0 idle, 1 send an ordinary request, 2 send a protected request, 3 service the request in one's inbox, and 4 timeout/reset one's sending window. Each agent has two transmission credits. A send consumes one credit, inserts the privately observed demand value in outbound slot 0 and replaces that demand with a keyed random draw in [0.4, 1.0]. The packet advances to slot 1 on the next transition, then attempts to enter the other agent's inbox on the following transition. Thus the sender cannot directly finish its own request.

gi070.title: Cross-pollination with delayed yield and a shared aquifer
gi070.summary: Each agent privately observes its own fixed variety preference, planted variety and crop health. Public signals include both nutrient reserves, growth, planted/empty indicators, previous actions and realized harvest values, together with weather and aquifer level. Incoming pollen reveals the emitted variety. Previous planting actions are public, so the partner's variety can be reconstructed from history; it is not claimed to remain secret. The other's fixed preference and health are not direct observation columns.

gi071.title: Coupled clutches on an inertial shared carrier
gi071.summary: Each agent has its own current target from four interior positions. A delivery requires the carrier to be near that target at low speed. On delivery, that agent alone draws one of the other three targets using the explicit key. Targets may coincide or conflict. Motor and carrier dynamics are public; each agent directly sees only its own target. Delivery indicator lights and previous actions are public, so actions and outcomes may support inference about the other's task. There is no observation column containing the other target.

gi072.title: Twin-Grip Lockway
gi072.summary: Bring the shared pallet to [14,5] and all three workers into x>=12.

gi073.title: Chromatic Switchyard
gi073.summary: Complete all four receivers' ordered three-colour demands using the finite 8-blue/8-amber source.

gi074.title: Cinderline Commons
gi074.summary: Extinguish all fire while preserving all three seedbeds, using spatial resupply, cooling, fuel removal and repair.

gi075.title: Scentbank Scramble
gi075.summary: Bank the six autonomous neutral grazers for one's own team using position, attraction/repulsion pucks and a teammate's bench settling.

gi076.title: Ballast Run — The Drifting Sample Skiff
gi076.summary: A three-person crew must collect three fragile survey capsules from marked river buoys and bank them at its home berth. The skiff retains velocity until counter-thrust or braking changes it. Walking crew, filled corner tanks and loaded capsules change its balance; loose capsules slide toward the low edge and can be lost. Two reusable clips can secure capsules, while cliffs, reef collision and severe imbalance damage the hull.

gi077.title: Veinbound
gi077.summary: Two rival two-person survey crews hunt eight buried geodes. A surveyor can measure counts of amber and teal deposits within a radius but cannot see their exact positions. An excavator opens soil faster. Private scan records can be exchanged only when teammates meet. Once exposed, a geode can be carried, deliberately handed off by dropping it, or knocked loose by a rival's shove. Banking preferred-colour geodes is worth more; the first team to reach eight points wins, with simultaneous finishes resolved from the same new state.

gi078.title: Thawforge Caravan | Three hands, one warm workshop
gi078.summary: Keep all three crew warm, manufacture three plates and two gaskets, install them into the rescue beacon, and operate it with at least two adjacent crew for three consecutive effective charge steps while the shared hearth has fuel.

gi079.title: Switchback Relay | Cover the breach, bring the core home
gi079.summary: Maintain a passable relay gate, retrieve the physical core from the turret bay, and bring it to the extraction cell (1,4) with positive hull and at least one surviving squad member.

gi080.title: Canal Charters | A board of water, rights and consequences
gi080.summary: Earn own-farm harvests and access income while constructing and scheduling the shared canal network. Collective completion occurs when every farm has three harvests before flood closure.

gi081.title: Dockside Promises | Right-of-way is a costly promise
gi081.summary: Deliver two physically carried orders per courier before their deadlines, balancing private timeliness against shared traffic, charging, route commitments and energy assistance.

gi082.title: Lantern Flood
gi082.summary: Carry two casualties to Manhattan distance at most one from the depot. Each delivery gives all roles +1 and each expiry gives all roles -1.

gi083.title: Relay Bastions
gi083.summary: Owned uncontested nodes pay every fourth step, weighted top 1, center 2, bottom 1. Both teammates receive own-team minus opponent point increments; opposing team receives the negative.

gi084.title: Thermal Loom
gi084.summary: Cooperatively ship three of four original pieces. Each shipment gives every role +1; each thermal spoil gives every role -1. Intermediate progress has no shaping reward.

gi085.title: Cipher Causeway
gi085.summary: Runners recover cipher and carry it to exact exit tile; wardens seek both runners restrained first. Extraction pays each runner +1 and each warden -1; both-captured reverses rewards. Unresolved horizon pays zero.

gi086.title: Lockstep Gantry
gi086.summary: Deliver the actual three-cell beam horizontally with center [10,4] before a jam or the 80-step bound.

gi087.title: Spillway Orchard
gi087.summary: Before 96 steps, keep enough of the commons alive for every role to bank at least four fruit; individuals also earn private harvest and bank rewards.

gi088.title: Borrowed Current
gi088.summary: All three operators must complete two services before 96 steps while supplying and traversing the shared network.

gi089.title: Lantern Intercept
gi089.summary: Bring the single relic to your team base with your runner carrying and your scout simultaneously co-signing nearby, while the other team can intercept.

gi090.title: Relayline: The Four-Tick Ball
gi090.summary: Two teams of two compete to carry the ball into their own far goal after a teammate has caught a pass during the current possession.

gi091.title: Ember Weir: Shared Firebreaks
gi091.summary: Contain two spreading fire fronts while preserving at least one of three shared assets, using finite water, temporary firebreaks and teammate transfers.

gi092.title: Lumen Locks: Cross-Wired Signals
gi092.summary: Deliver both physical cargo objects from the east loading bay to the northern goal, using two cross-wired remote gate operators and brief binary broadcasts.

gi093.title: Trestle Commons: Roads and Rivalry
gi093.summary: Move each role's actual cart from the western bank to its matching eastern goal, while deciding whether to pool construction resources, share bridges, maintain access or pursue toll income.

gi094.title: Three-Hand Kiln
gi094.summary: Cooperate to complete the public sequence of four flavor-specific orders using physical raw ingredients, two cleaver work units, four oven ticks and delivery at dispatch.

gi095.title: Copper Relay
gi095.summary: Two pairs of teammates compete to accumulate 12 relay pulses through physically adjacent supply conduits. Both relay sites may be captured by either team.

gi096.title: Flank-and-Hold Meadow
gi096.summary: Cooperate to guide four physical animals through the gate to either safe pen while limiting panic and ditch losses.

gi097.title: Lockwake Convoys
gi097.summary: Transport three physical cargo contracts through a shared narrow canal. Each contract owner receives its own outcome while every role also shares part of every delivery or loss.

gi098.title: Prism Commons
gi098.summary: Charge all three receivers to three. Each role gains more from its own receiver; launch credit and the shared completion bonus create additional motives to assist.

gi099.title: Lantern Courtyard
gi099.summary: Wardens aim to immobilize every courier still inside. Couriers aim to get both pennants out, one carried pennant per escaping courier, while keeping their partner available for rescue.

gi100.title: Three Quays
gi100.summary: Each merchant needs two units of its required kind at its own depot. Initially nobody owns the kind they need. Negotiate through visible recipient quotes, physical deposits, conditional cycles or unsecured gifts, then transport the newly owned goods.

gi101.title: Counterweight Yard
gi101.summary: Install one block at each side station and two at the middle station. Cargo cannot be carried upward on ladders; raise it on shared lifts. Build a bridge to support the middle station. A station's corresponding role earns the larger installation bonus even when another worker carries the material.

gi102.title: Signal Veil Relay
gi102.summary: Two teams capture the enemy physical beacon and carry it onto their own base while their own beacon is on its home tile and uncarried.

gi103.title: Switchback Repair Crew
gi103.summary: Repair the bridge console, prime the pump and restore the transmitter using the one wrench, one power cell and complementary worker capabilities.

gi104.title: Orchard Watershed Commons
gi104.summary: Each steward deposits six fruits at their own storehouse while preserving or restoring the shared orchard network; fruit can instead be invested or gifted.

gi105.title: Two-Stride Relay Arena
gi105.summary: Two teams relay a physical token through space. An allied in-flight catch arms scoring; carry the armed token onto your three-cell target goal.

gi106.title: Hose Relay: Firebreak Rescue
gi106.summary: Rescue six evacuees before accumulating three severe-fire exposures, using shared water, hose infrastructure and firebreaks.

gi107.title: Counterweight Crossing
gi107.summary: Deliver all four evacuees and evacuate all three responders to the east shelter, preserving access while others cross.

gi108.title: Escrow Street Market
gi108.summary: Complete each trader's own private two-unit delivery order while managing finite capacity, barter commitments and competing demand for scarce surplus.

gi109.title: Whisper Corridors
gi109.summary: Roles 0/1 coordinate to deliver the parcel through one of two exits; roles 2/3 coordinate to intercept. Scouts provide expiring route intelligence and operate corridor gates.

gi110.title: Tugboat Convoy: Two Channels, One Hydraulic Selector
gi110.summary: Deliver barge 0 to (8,2) and barge 1 to (8,6). Each new delivery pays every tug +1; every sanitized non-wait action costs that tug 1/64. No reward is attached to cooperation labels.

gi111.title: Counter-Signal Garden: Relay, Guard and Disrupt

gi112.title: Shared-Heat Workshop: Three Specialists, Two Conserved Workpieces
gi112.summary: Forge, temper, assemble and physically ship both workpieces. A new fully shipped piece pays every specialist +1; any non-wait legal action costs its actor 1/128. Intermediate stages do not pay delivery reward.

gi113.title: Courier Commitments: Escrow Bridge and Private Delivery Orders
gi113.summary: Route physical parcels to each owner private depot requirement. Delivery pays its beneficiary +1 and actual delivering courier +1/4. Actual bridge payments cost payer amount/16 reward; non-wait actions cost actor 1/128.

gi115.title: Freight canal locks and shared water
gi115.summary: Deliver each boat cargo to its indexed dock using either lock lane and the two shared transferable water units.

gi116.title: Bridge builders with unequal tool kits
gi116.summary: Bring all three crew members to x>=6 across two channels using four reusable parts and temporary spans.

gi117.title: Hidden-demand exchange yard
gi117.summary: Each trader delivers two goods of its private required type to its own dock. Exactly two physical goods of each type exist.

gi118.title: Sailboat race with shared wind shadows

gi119.title: Circuit crews with coupled power paths
gi119.summary: Repair both facilities to four units by transporting and installing limited cables, switches and batteries. Every crew member receives total actual repair increment divided by eight.

gi120.title: Territorial patrol and mobile decoys
gi120.summary: Two teams contest four physical objectives and transport them to their own homes. Team rewards oppose each other for deliveries and actual captures; teammates share their team payoff.

gi121.title: Orchard pollination and shared habitat
gi121.summary: Each grower earns fruit only from ripe own plots. They share three mobile pollinators, three circulating seeds and 22 initial water units, creating individual incentives to coordinate flowering and habitat care while competing for resources and six season harvest slots.

gi122.title: Tether Turn — three ports and a shared bulky load
gi122.summary: Cooperatively deliver the three-cell load to center (10,5) with horizontal footprint.

gi123.title: Echo Passage — lures, patrols and shared exposure
gi123.summary: Return both mission cases to the public western extraction point before alarm failure or H=112.

gi124.title: Bankline — four-player ricochet possession arena
gi124.summary: With a teammate, pass, shoot, block and intercept a shared ball to score three goals before the opponent.

gi125.title: Common Kiln — private orders in a coupled workshop
gi125.summary: Fulfil three distinct private workshop orders using conserved raw stock, shared heat, cooling, a press and one transport/handling tool.

gi126.title: Bridgewrights: Hold the Span
gi126.summary: Deliver each worker's personal cargo to its exact opposite-bank flag, while maintaining shared crossing structures.

gi127.title: Shield Relay: Escort the Supply Line
gi127.summary: Escort two living supply carts to the east edge while allocating directional shielding, energy, repairs and movement.

gi128.title: Crossbar Couriers: Pass Before Expiry
gi128.summary: Carry or relay four expiring packets to their privately assigned opposite-side depots through three shared openings.

gi129.title: Shepherd Circles: Two Gates, One Flock
gi129.summary: Guide all six sheep through timed fence gates into their matching upper or lower pen using combined spatial pressure and temporary calls.

gi130.title: Sluice Commons and Downstream Passage
gi130.summary: Deliver the three finite cargo boats to basin 3 while irrigating each indexed crop twice or recording its loss. Each role benefits especially from its same-index cargo and crop; sharing and bridge access affect all roles.

gi131.title: Firebreak Crews and Shared Rescue Routes
gi131.summary: Rescue six individually conserved survivors while protecting crews and managing finite water. Every rescue has shared value and extra value to its actual rescuer and the survivor-index priority role.

gi132.title: Lightkeepers and Shared Shadow Corridors
gi132.summary: Retrieve the three finite coded caches under real illumination and carry them to the central socket, while retaining safe shadow crossings and enough shared lamp charge. Cache owners have different delivery deadlines.

gi133.title: Conveyor Workshop and Synchronized Assembly
gi133.summary: Use six finite parts to satisfy three chassis-plus-coil orders, reworking defects and matching requested coil colors, then physically carry valid products to the dock before their role-linked deadlines when possible.

gi134.title: Tide Ledger: Salvage Claims
gi134.summary: Deliver three salvage lots through shared bottlenecks. Individual delivery values compete with auction costs; every delivery also benefits all three salvagers.

gi135.title: Nine Shards Council
gi135.summary: Cooperatively fill the nine mosaic cells with their hidden target colours, using exactly nine finite tiles, spatial access, public hints and transfers.

gi136.title: Turnhouse Compact
gi136.summary: Transport the three owner-specific cargo items to their assigned bays, then escape. Physical couriers may deliver another owner's cargo, and their rotations can enable or obstruct partners.

gi137.title: Mossline Pursuit
gi137.summary: Trackers 0 and 1 cooperate to tag runners before extraction. Runners 2 and 3 cooperate to reach either exit, using hiding, shared-trail erasure and decoys with finite charges.

gi138.title: Switchback Relay
gi138.summary: Two teams contest one ball. A team wins by carrying a relayed ball into its opposite-end strip; direct solo carries cannot score.

gi139.title: Three Bloom Exchange
gi139.summary: Cooperatively deliver the six finite fruits. Each delivery rewards every courier 0.5; the delivering courier additionally receives 0.5 when its private preferred species matches.

gi140.title: Two-bank Trestle
gi140.summary: Use three beams and two reusable clamps to carry the single heavy crate from the west bank to within one cell of (8,3). Successful delivery rewards every role +1.

gi141.title: Lantern Strait
gi141.summary: Deliver each vessel's parcel to its private berth on the opposite bank. Own completion pays 0.75 plus a public 0.25 per completion to every role, creating both urgency and shared benefit.

gi142.title: Lantern Flag Rescue
gi142.summary: Return the enemy flag to the carrier team base while the carrier team own flag is on its home base. Team 0 is agents 0,1; team 1 is agents 2,3.

gi143.title: Crosswake Ice Doubles
gi143.summary: Two teams contest two neutral stones. Entering the right goal (x=10,y=2..4) scores team 0; entering the left goal (x=0,y=2..4) scores team 1, regardless of last pusher.

gi144.title: Phase-Lock Relay
gi144.summary: Deliver cargo 0 from (1,1) to (9,1) and cargo 1 from (1,5) to (9,5), using periodic gates and distributed local station commands.

gi145.title: Breathshare Claims
gi145.summary: Bring finite ore to (1,3). Each miner privately values one randomly assigned ore type; all share delivery benefits and survival losses. Maintain oxygen using two portable canisters and finite shared station stock.

gi146.title: Firebreak Pumps and Shared Evacuation
gi146.summary: Evacuate both occupants at the refuge before either suffers fatal heat exposure; share the finite water supply.

gi147.title: Harbor Barter and Complementary Cargo
gi147.summary: Fulfil the boat's private two-type delivery demand by consensual cargo exchange and use of two congested shared docks.

gi148.title: Echo Hunt and Distributed Local Sensing
gi148.summary: Scouts coordinate local sensors, finite pulses, physical beacons and tags to capture the two player-controlled runners; runners use routes, smoke, jams and exits.

gi149.title: Tide Locks and Competitive Salvage Crews
gi149.summary: Each two-role crew competes for a majority of three movable salvage crates while using shared tidal locks.

gi150.title: Relay Foundry
gi150.summary: Complete four finite serial orders in FIFO order by relaying parts through three complementary manufacturing capabilities and one shared portable clamp.

gi151.title: Common Meadow
gi151.summary: Individually bank three harvested tufts while preserving a viable shared meadow; decide when to extract, restore, protect, donate and move away from crowded patches.

gi152.title: Lane Relay Gridball
gi152.summary: Two teammates create passing and shooting lanes against two opponents; score three goals before the opposing team while managing stamina and possession.

gi153.title: Bonded Bridges
gi153.summary: Transport four complementary parcels to their bilateral private target depots by negotiating scarce expiring bridge access; choose toll revenue, prompt passage and reciprocal delivery assistance.

gi154.title: Island Spark
gi154.summary: Restore and operate a small fictional grid to service three units at each of two sinks, balancing portable charge, spatial repair access and shared line capacity.

gi155.title: Echo Tow
gi155.summary: Recover two heavy cargo objects at matching berths by coordinating two attached tugs, scout information, current diversion and shared oxygen resupply.

gi156.title: Leeward Caravan
gi156.summary: Deliver one heavy load across a ridge using synchronized hauling, movable wind shelter, finite water and interchangeable transport/support roles.

gi157.title: Ghostlight Tag
gi157.summary: Coordinate beacon control, cover, pursuit, decoy placement and rescues to capture both opposing players simultaneously.

gi158.title: Pressure Relay
gi158.summary: Bring both fragile artifacts to the west dock while keeping every crew member breathing.

gi159.title: Sealed Routes
gi159.summary: Earn parcel value and relay fees by delivering parcels to their true depots; use contingent commitments and scarce one-parcel capacity.

gi160.title: Railguard
gi160.summary: Your two-player team incapacitates both opponents while using shared shields, ammunition and rescues to remain active.

gi161.title: Tetherwake
gi161.summary: Recover each salvage module at its assigned western dock while choosing when to help, anchor, recharge or collect personal chips.

gi162.title: Canal Commons
gi162.summary: Harvest the assigned crop while deciding how much finite upstream water and personal effort to spend on shared canal service and neighbours.

gi163.title: Beacon Convoy
gi163.summary: Deliver personal cargo through a two-route corridor while deciding whether to trust claims, spend fuel on escort/aid, and honour costly commitments.

gi164.title: Workshop Exchange
gi164.summary: Use complementary specialist production and local escrow trades to complete shared machines, or take immediate private component-sale rewards.

gi165.title: Crossing Accord
gi165.summary: Coordinate two couriers per team to deliver across the river while controlling, diverting, yielding or blocking routes and contesting energy-saving switch plazas.

gi166.title: Switchyard Claims
gi166.summary: Deliver each controlled train cargo at the single depot while trading own urgency costs against competing track access.

gi167.title: Echo Pursuit
gi167.summary: Two controlled hunters seek a capture; the controlled evader seeks an explicit gate escape after tick eight. Scans exchange energy and concealment for imperfect persistent contacts.

gi168.title: Lifeline Grid
gi168.summary: Provide each service site 24 units while maintainers balance private service value, shared reliability, finite repair stock and finite reserve.

gi169.title: Mutual Cover
gi169.summary: Move finite cargo to own destination while choosing cash expenditure, safer spatial routes, protection, escort, repairs and credible collateralized cover.

gi170.title: Counterweight Crew
gi170.summary: Deliver three salvage cargoes. Rewards equal individual public depot values times cargo weight less directional effort.

gi171.title: Shared Firebreak
gi171.summary: Limit three-asset damage using finite labor, water, shared refills, gifts and permanent firebreaks. Each crew privately values one asset four and other assets one.

gi172.title: Signal Bargain
gi172.summary: Collect complementary goods, explicitly exchange them through spatial escrow contracts, and deliver up to two private recipes at own home before the role deadline.

gi173.title: Relay Arena
gi173.summary: Pairs 0/1 and 2/3 attack right and left goals using controlled carrying, directional passing, receiving, interception and screening.

gi174.title: Floodgate Commons
gi174.summary: Each controlled keeper values its own harvests and must balance its water supply with shared flood prevention and downstream access.

gi175.title: Lantern Convoy
gi175.summary: Transport fragile cargo to its matching destination while choosing who carries cargo, who pays finite illumination and which stale reports to share.

gi176.title: Charter Frontier
gi176.summary: Claim one privately useful frontier plot, construct with finite materials and collect harvests; voluntarily finance and vote on temporary shared corridor access.

gi177.title: Tag Exchange
gi177.summary: Each controlled pair captures the opposing flag while preserving its own flag at home, coordinating tags, rescue, handoff and finite recharge.

gi178.title: Orbit Salvage
gi178.summary: Deliver the shared salvage to either exact dock while stopped and attached to at least two tugs; each tug values one destination more.

gi179.title: Filter Couriers
gi179.summary: Deliver three distinct loads to their designated stations while preserving quality; original issuers earn private priority-weighted quality and the actual carrier earns a handling bonus.

gi180.title: Beacon Auction
gi180.summary: Each courier delivers once to either terminal across the partition; finite charge may be spent on access rights, tolls, a bypass or partner assistance. Fixed pairs are (0,1) and (2,3).

gi181.title: Bridge Pact
gi181.summary: Build and maintain real capacity-one multi-cell crossings to deliver each parcel across separated islands; either north or south terminal pays a private value.

gi182.title: Rhythm Foundry
gi182.summary: Process finite ingredients and ship physical goods; each worker values its private preferred furnace more and shares each shipment bonus.

gi183.title: Mist Runners
gi183.summary: Two teams carry their finite native packets to the opposing base. Deliveries reward both teammates and penalize the opposing team; tagging, sensing and covering can alter the race.

gi184.title: Rotating Keep
gi184.summary: Each actor claims one destination and may then keep helping. Matching its private preference yields the larger individual reward; every claim also benefits peers.

gi185.title: Mosaic Courtyard
gi185.summary: Construct traversable patterned paths and physically reach and commission a socket. Private destination preferences and shared claim bonuses shape which paths actors favor.

gi186.title: Floodstone Builders
gi186.summary: Extract and bank the three distinct finite ore units while preserving miners and infrastructure; preferred-vein bonus creates individual interests.

gi187.title: Ember Shelter
gi187.summary: Survive three finite day/night cycles by building and maintaining a shared insulated, fueled shelter; balance communal materials against individual private stash priorities.

gi188.title: Canal Kitchen
gi188.summary: Prepare chopped vegetables and cooked broth, assemble and serve four timed meals, and circulate the two finite bowls across a canal.

gi189.title: Night Market Crew
gi189.summary: Resolve six market orders with shared heat, finite water and a three-utensil cleaning circuit; choose hot or discounted cold service and balance private dish priorities.

gi190.title: River Charter
gi190.summary: Manage a finite eight-flood river economy. Earn personal utility by eating grain or exporting it, while diversion, bridge access and shipments change other polities resources and opportunities.

gi191.title: Border Loom
gi191.summary: Sell four finite hometown commodities at the next roles town. Build a useful shared transport network while bargaining over toll revenue and temporary reciprocal access.

gi192.title: Orchard Commons
gi192.summary: Grow and sell orchard fruit through six growth ticks. Coordinate scarce water, pollinating habitat and one shared pruning tool while choosing crops for private tastes and alternating market demand.

gi193.title: Village Loom
gi193.summary: Supply two cloth orders per villager before the fair closes. Growing flax, borrowing tools, exchanging material, repairing shared machines and committing labor all compete with private delivery deadlines.

gi194.title: Windlift Quarry
gi194.summary: Deliver all six individually owned ore blocks to their matching top-row depots while choosing between shared lift service and long edge ramps.

gi195.title: Clockwork Banquet
gi195.summary: Serve four banquet courses in order vegetable, protein, vegetable, protein using three reusable trays and three ingredients of each type.

gi196.title: Beacon Marches
gi196.summary: Supply each polity's opposite-bank outpost twice before any outpost defense reaches zero; manage couriers, fuel, relay information and timed passage agreements.

gi197.title: Meadow Rotations
gi197.summary: Deliver at least two milk portions from each of three herd owners to the shared barn before a herd loses all health; maintain grazing access, water and repairable gates.

gi198.title: Tideworks Yard
gi198.summary: Deliver all six construction crates while building, sharing, anchoring or drifting real pontoon routes across the harbor channel.

gi199.title: Icehouse Service
gi199.summary: Serve two hot courses and two chilled desserts using three trays, six total ingredients, two portable ice boxes and a finite cooling/fuel reserve.

gi200.title: Signal Coast League
gi200.summary: Deliver two supplies for each polity while scouting, paying finite signal costs, interpreting expiring warnings, and committing caravans to safe-stop road segments.

gi201.title: Canopy Commons
gi201.summary: Deliver six total fruit portions through individual owner stalls or the community barn while growing saplings, managing shade, water and finite planting beds.

gi202.title: Counterweight Foundry
gi202.summary: Deliver all three tagged crates by loading the beam and bringing both ends to row seven.

gi203.title: Proofing House
gi203.summary: Serve two plain and two seeded loaves from finite ingredients using the three reusable trays.

gi204.title: Treaty Rail
gi204.summary: Deliver at least two cargo units from each settlement's finite supply to the public depot while managing signals, passing loops and three lendable wagons.

gi205.title: Pollinator Paths
gi205.summary: Bring six produce units to the community barn while tending shared pollination routes, moisture and finite planting resources.

gi206.title: Echo Quarry
gi206.summary: Expose and deliver all six owner-tagged parcels without fatal collapse.

gi207.title: Steam Basket Kitchen
gi207.summary: Serve two vegetable and two dense baskets using finite ingredients, wrappers, fuel and wash water.

gi208.title: Canal Compact
gi208.summary: Deliver each settlement's single cargo to its destination while choosing how much finite local water to spend on passage versus private crops.

gi209.title: Compost Commons

v1_000.title: Window v1 · Delayed pledges with endogenous credibility
v1_000.summary: Delayed pledges with endogenous credibility. Actions open a three-transition promise, supply two units of work, endorse the other agent with escrow, or withdraw. At maturity a completed promise benefits its recipient in proportion to the sender's accumulated credibility and endorsement; failures damage that recipient and reduce sender credibility. Endorsement is costly and increases exposure. The work clock and endorsement timing create action-history dependence. Both agents can change the other's delayed payout and their own persistent credibility. All states are initialized; work, trust and escrow are bounded. tanh maps the finite sum of delivery, failure and effort terms into [-1,1]. Constant all-legal actions include ineffective actions when their prerequisite is absent. No effectiveness or equilibrium claim has been tested.

v1_001.title: Window v1 · Renewing commons with delayed runoff
v1_001.summary: A shared renewing stock with a two-slot runoff pipeline. Gentle and deep extraction compete proportionally for the same current stock. Only deep extraction creates runoff, mitigated by the extractor's decaying private filter. Runoff affects soil after the pipeline delay; soil determines future resource renewal. Tending repairs shared soil while filter investment changes future individual externalities. The common stock, soil and pipeline couple both agents persistently, unlike a promise clock. Reward is tanh of current allocated yield minus tending/filter costs and arriving shared pollution. Allocation and all continuous stocks are bounded, making the reward finite and within [-1,1]. No policy benefit has been evaluated.

v1_002.title: Window v1 · Manufacturing and persistent custom offers
v1_002.summary: Trade opportunities are produced by action, not supplied as fixed random meetings. Manufacturing creates stock at a rate determined by tools. An offer posted after manufacturing lasts across multiple transitions; a later partner acceptance consumes a unit from the seller, pays seller and buyer, and upgrades buyer tools. A buyer can first create a custom order, at cost, then later satisfy it via trade for an additional payoff. Partner custom orders also improve producer tooling. Simultaneous decisions accept only previously visible offers, preventing same-step retroactive opportunities. Stocks, offer lifetimes, tools and orders are bounded. tanh of finite buyer/seller gains, order completion and production/order costs is in [-1,1]. Both agents alter the other's inventory and future productive capacity. The mechanism is untested scientifically.

v1_003.title: Window v1 · Private revelation and directional mode pressure
v1_003.summary: Private revelation and directional manipulation of a hidden transition mode. Projects mature two transitions after initiation and pay according to the mode at completion, not at initiation. A costly probe reveals only the probing agent's post-transition mode and stores an aging private signal. Costly pushes create persistent signed pressure: agent zero pushes toward zero, agent one toward one; sufficient pressure overrides random mode drift. Project types are private while project timers, pressure and realized outcomes are public. The other agent's push can invalidate a stale observation and change a pending project's payoff. Mode, pressure, timers and signal age are bounded. tanh maps finite completion payoffs and action costs into [-1,1]. Randomness uses only the supplied explicit key. Information value, strategic advantage and learning performance remain untested.
